title: Discord client data
whyItMatters: Discord caches servers, direct messages and attachments and keeps a login token locally. The token is enough to take over the account until the password is changed.
source: Discord desktop is an Electron app that stores its user data in the app-data folder (leveldb caches, logs): https://github.com/discord/discord-api-docs
notes: Stable client. Discord Canary, PTB and Development builds use discordcanary, discordptb and discorddevelopment folders next to it. Versioned folders under discord hold the app itself.

cleanup.exportFirst: Save any file or message you need from Discord first, because the local cache is all that is removed here.
cleanup.signOut: In Discord, open User Settings > Authorized Apps and deauthorize apps you no longer use, then sign out of the app.
steps: Uninstall Discord from Settings > Apps > Installed apps.
Delete the Discord folder named in the plan if it is still there.
cleanup.risk: Removes cached messages, attachments and the local login token; the account stays until the password is changed.
cleanup.source: Discord Support, My Discord Account was Hacked or Compromised: https://support.discord.com/hc/en-us/articles/24160905919511-My-Discord-Account-was-Hacked-or-Compromised
